content: The final hour of our life does not bring death, but only finishes it.
author: Seneca
sourceWork: De Tranquillitate Animi (On Tranquility of Mind)
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

Across his life and work, Seneca saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: What long-held assumption about your life or abilities is challenged by this insight?
